title: 1998 FIFA World Cup
prose:
The 1998 FIFA World Cup, staged in France from 10 June to 12 July, marked a turning point in the tournament's scale. For the first time the field expanded from 24 to 32 teams, drawn into eight groups of four. The top two from each group advanced to a single-elimination knockout phase running from the round of 16 through the quarter-finals, semi-finals and final. In all, 64 matches were played across 10 stadiums, drawing a total attendance of 2,785,100 spectators at an average of 43,517 per game. The expanded format opened the door to debutants Croatia, Jamaica, Japan and South Africa, and the tournament introduced the golden goal rule in the knockout stage.

The hosts surged through the knockout rounds, winning every match they played to reach the final at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, just outside Paris. There they met Brazil, the holders and the tournament's most feared side. The match was shaped before kick-off by an extraordinary subplot: Ronaldo, Brazil's star and the eventual Golden Ball winner as best player, suffered a convulsive fit on the afternoon of the final and was briefly left off the team sheet before being reinstated. He played but was subdued, fuelling a controversy that endures to this day.

France seized the occasion through Zinedine Zidane, who scored twice with first-half headers, in the 27th minute and in first-half stoppage time (45+1'). Emmanuel Petit added a third in stoppage time (90+3') to seal a 3-0 victory in regular time, with no extra time or penalties required. France were champions, Brazil the runners-up.

The triumph made France the seventh nation to win the World Cup and the sixth to lift it on home soil, their first title. Elsewhere, Croatia announced itself emphatically, reaching the semi-finals in its first World Cup as an independent nation and finishing third by beating the fourth-placed Netherlands 2-1 in the third-place match. Croatia's Davor Suker crowned the tournament as its top scorer with six goals, claiming the Golden Boot.
